title: Red Alert in Six Odisha Districts as Cyclone Arnab Heads for October 28 Landfall
excerpt: The IMD now expects a very severe cyclonic storm to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with gusts to 140 km/h; Odisha has mobilised 225 rescue teams and cancelled disaster staff leave.
body:
• The IMD has upgraded its warning: the Bay of Bengal system is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on the forenoon of October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with winds of 115-125 km/h gusting to 140 km/h.
  • A red warning is in force for six Odisha districts — Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri — with the heaviest impact expected between Kakinada and Gopalpur.
  • Odisha has cancelled leave for disaster personnel and mobilised 225 rescue teams; Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi says the target is zero casualties.
  • What this means for you: fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea, and families in coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha should expect extremely heavy rainfall on October 27-28 and follow district evacuation orders.

The India Meteorological Department has raised its warning for the Bay of Bengal system — to be named Cyclone Arnab — saying it will intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28. Manorama Mohanty, director of the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar, told ANI the depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal would become a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26 and a severe cyclonic storm on October 27, before reaching the west-central Bay near the Andhra coast on the morning of October 28, according to NDTV.

Where and how hard it will hit

The IMD expects the storm to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28, with sustained winds of 115 to 125 km/h gusting to 140 km/h. Landfall is in Andhra Pradesh, but officials say the rainfall impact on Odisha will be more significant than the wind: a red warning covers Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts, and the stretch between Kakinada and Gopalpur is expected to take the greatest impact. Coastal Andhra Pradesh faces extremely heavy rainfall on October 27 and 28, and Odisha on October 28.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2114397450597548337

"We have assigned specific responsibilities to each department, ensuring they are fully prepared in advance. The state government is completely ready to handle this situation. As always, our primary objective remains the same: zero casualties."

— Mohan Charan Majhi, Chief Minister of Odisha

The response on the ground

Odisha has cancelled the leave of all disaster personnel and placed 225 rescue teams on high alert across vulnerable districts, according to ANI reporting. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed preparations on Sunday and said the system is expected to make landfall on the afternoon of October 28 somewhere between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, bringing heavy rainfall across districts in both states, as reported by The Times of Bengal. Fishermen have been strictly advised not to venture into the sea, and government holidays in affected areas have been cancelled. Andhra and Odisha had already activated their disaster machinery earlier in the weekend; President Murmu's Odisha visit has been put off to November 4-5 because of the storm.

What happens next

The next 48 hours are the escalation window: cyclonic storm by October 26, severe by October 27, and landfall on October 28. Forecasters stress that the exact track can still shift, which would move the heaviest rain between coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. Residents in the red-warning districts should treat October 27 as the last full day to prepare, and diaspora families with relatives along the Kakinada-Gopalpur stretch should check in before communications are disrupted at landfall.
